newsitem.title: USA: Pier 1 sees Nov same-store sales up.
newsitem.headline: Pier 1 sees Nov same-store sales up.

text.p: Pier 1 Imports Inc said on Wednesday it expected November same-store sales to be above November same-store sales last year, which rose 12.6 percent.
"We had an utterly fabulous weekend after Thanksgiving," Chairman Clark Johnson told an analysts' meeting.
"Last December, our comps were up 16.1 percent so we're up against a hurdle, but based on the way things look now we are going to have another extraordinarily good Christmas."
Johnson also said management was confortable with analysts' earnings estimates between $0.96 per share and $1.00 per share for fiscal 1997.
In fiscal 1998, Pier 1 would see a "material lift" in earnings due to debt reduction, Johnson said.

In July, Pier 1 converted $68.3 million of its 6-7/8 percent subordinated convertible debentures and in September it completed a public offering of $75 million in 5-3/4 percent convertible subordinated notes.
Proceeds from the offering were used to retire high-cost debt, the company said.
Johnson said Pier 1 sales year-to-date were up about 14.5 percent and comparable sales were up about 10.5 percent.

Pier 1's results were being boosted by market share gains, strong systems and expense control, its direct importing strategy and the ability to sustain above average store expansion in a difficult real estate environment, he said.
There was also a growing trend toward home furnishings purchases, the company said.
"Home furnishings have come into their own," Johnson said.
"The 80s were the 'me' decade and the 90s are the 'we' decade. People are spending more money on their homes," he said.
In keeping with this trend, Pier 1 said it aimed to completely exit the apparel business by May of next year.
This would open up seven percent of additional square footage in stores, Johnson said.

Longer term, the company said its goal was to grow its top line 12 to 15 percent annually over the next five years. Johnson said Pier 1 would achieve this by steadily growing same-store sales six to seven percent a year over the period.
Pier 1 also said it hoped to grow its bottom line 15 to 18 percent annually over the next five years.
To this goal, Johnson said Pier 1 expected gross profit margins to rise and an ongoing international freight rate war to continue, because of available container space.
He said television advertising which promoted the brand, compared with print circulars which only promoted items, would also help the bottom line and attract new customers.
New products, new customers and new products would bolster same-store sales growth, Johnson said.
The company planned to remodel 50 stores a year, and it had a "remerchandising" program, which included discontinuing its apparel line and selling more high-quality items, he said.
In fiscal 1998, Johnson said Pier 1 would remerchandise 143 stores and remodel 50 of its stores.
It also aimed to expand internationally by one to two percent a year, the company said.
